title: Optimization of a new selective pressurized liquid extraction methodology for determining organic pollutants in wild boar livers
author: González-Gómez, Cambeiro-Pérez, et al.
materials: A list of the target OPs and the labelled internal and surrogate standards including CAS and supplier is given in Table S1 and S2, respectively. In order to improve peak shape and reduce OP decomposition, the 3-ethoxy-1,2-propanediol (98 %), d-sorbitol (> 99 %) and l-gulonic acid γ-lactone (> 98 %) used as analyte protectants (APs) were purchased from Sigma Aldrich (Madrid, Spain). Individual stock standard solutions of APs were prepared in acetonitrile (50 g/L), acetonitrile:water (85:15, v/v, 5 g/L) and acetonitrile:water (80:20, v/v, 5 g/L), respectively. Mixes of 10 mg/L stock solutions of each family of OPs were prepared from the individual stock solutions standards in acetonitrile. From these solutions, standards ranging from 0.25 to 100 μg/L were prepared in APs and used to construct the calibration line. These solutions were stored in amber flasks at - 18°C.

steps.title: Prepare analyte protectant stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3‑ethoxy‑1,2‑propanediol (98 %) at 50 g L⁻¹ in acetonitrile; dissolve d‑sorbitol (>99 %) at 5 g L⁻¹ in acetonitrile:water 85:15 (v/v); dissolve l‑gulonic acid γ‑lactone (>98 %) at 5 g L⁻¹ in acetonitrile:water 80:20 (v/v). Store all AP stock solutions in amber flasks at –18 °C.

steps.title: Prepare OP stocks and calibrations
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mg L⁻¹ stock solutions of each OP family in acetonitrile. From these, make calibration standards ranging from 0.25 to 100 µg L⁻¹ in the AP mixture. Store the calibration solutions in amber flasks at –18 °C.

steps.title: Optimize additive combinations
steps.instruction: Test the effect of additives on 2.0 g liver samples spiked with OPs at 0.25 ng g⁻¹ and 0.50 ng g⁻¹. Evaluate aqueous KOH (30‑60 % w/v) and methanolic KOH (10‑35 % w/v) at volumes of 15 mL, 10 mL and 7.5 mL, together with activated silica amounts of 35 g, 30 g and 25 g. Record recoveries for each combination.

steps.title: Select optimal additive amounts
steps.instruction: Use 7.5 mL of KOH (60 % w/v), 35 g activated silica, and 1.0 g anhydrous sodium sulphate for each 2.0 g liver sample.

steps.title: Optimize extraction parameters
steps.instruction: Perform a Box‑Behnken design (15 random runs, three central‑point replicates) varying temperature (100 °C, 137.5 °C, 175 °C), static time (5 min, 10 min, 15 min) and pressure (100 ba, 125 ba, 150 ba) using acetonitrile as solvent. Determine the optimal condition as 100 °C, three extraction cycles of 10 min each, and 150 ba.

steps.title: Execute SPLE extraction
steps.instruction: Place the prepared liver sample (with additives) into the SPLE cell. Set the extractor to 100 °C, 150 ba, and run three consecutive 10‑minute extraction cycles with acetonitrile as the solvent. Collect the final acetonitrile extract (≈1.0 mL).

steps.title: Condition and load SPE cartridges
steps.instruction: Condition a tandem of dual‑layer EZ‑POP SPE cartridges with 20 mL acetone. Pass the 1.0 mL acetonitrile extract through the conditioned cartridges.

steps.title: Elute analytes and evaporate
steps.instruction: Elute the retained analytes from the SPE cartridges with 40 mL acetonitrile. Reduce the eluate to dryness in a rotary evaporator or nitrogen stream at 30 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute for GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Re‑dissolve the dried residue in 100 µL acetone containing 50 ng of the internal standards (DDT‑D8, diazinon‑D10, PCB 30 & 195, trans‑cypermethrin‑D6, PBDE 166) and the three APs. Vortex and transfer to GC‑MS vials.

steps.title: Run calibration and QA/QC samples
steps.instruction: Prepare a twelve‑point internal linear calibration (0.010–1.0 ng g⁻¹, r² > 0.999). Each analytical batch must include a reagent blank, a spiked blank, a spiked sample at 0.50 ng g⁻¹, and surrogate standards (chlorpyrifos‑D10, α,γ‑HCH‑D6, DDE‑D8, HCB‑13C6, Chrysene‑D12, PBDE 77, PCB 14, 65, 166, trans‑Permethrin‑D6) to monitor recovery.
